subject: Literacy
title: Making big marks
subtopics: Chalk and water on the ground
objectives: Children will make marks with fingers, chalk and crayons.
Children will say what their marks show.
content: Making marks in sand and flour, with chalk and water on the ground, and with crayons on big paper.
teachingActivities: Let children move freely with big arm movements; never correct how they hold a tool; ask "Tell me about your marks" and write down what they say; use large surfaces.
learnerActivities: Make marks with fingers, chalk and crayons and say what their marks show.
resources: A tray of sand or flour
A bucket of water and a brush
assessment: Observe whether each child makes marks with a tool and says a word about their marks.
expectedOutcomes: Says a word about their marks.

lessons.title: Marks in sand
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will make marks in sand or flour with their fingers.
successCriteria: Draws a line or a dot with a finger
Says a word about the mark
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can squeeze, roll and thread and enjoy exploring materials with their hands.
resources: A tray of dry sand or flour
lessons.starter: Draw a long line in the sand with your finger and say "I made a line. Can you make a mark?"
teacherActivities: Smooth the sand flat and draw a line, a dot and a circle with your finger.
Say "Now you make a mark." Give each child a turn.
Ask "What is your mark?" and wait.
Smooth the sand again and let the children make more marks.
learnerActivities: Children watch and look at the marks.
Child makes a mark with a finger.
Child says a word or shows a gesture.
Child makes a new mark.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Smooth the sand flat and draw a line, a dot and a circle with your finger. Children: Children watch and look at the marks.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Now you make a mark." Give each child a turn. Children: Child makes a mark with a finger.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What is your mark?" and wait. Children: Child says a word or shows a gesture.
Step 4. Teacher: Smooth the sand again and let the children make more marks. Children: Child makes a new mark.

practical.title: Sand marks
steps: Put a tray of sand on a table or mat.
Each child makes marks with a finger.
Smooth the sand and start again.
practical.safety: Keep sand away from eyes and mouths and wash hands after play. Use fine, clean sand and sweep up spills.

differentiation.support: Move the child’s finger along the sand together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a line and a circle and tell a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you make a long line?

expectedOutcomes: Makes marks in sand with a finger
Says a word about the mark
lessons.conclusion: Smooth the sand flat and wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Draw lines in sand or flour with your child at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make marks in sand or flour with their fingers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Chalk and water
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Chalk and water on the ground
objectives: Children will make big marks with chalk and water on the ground.
successCriteria: Uses chalk or a wet brush to make marks
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can squeeze, roll and thread and enjoy exploring materials with their hands.
resources: A bucket of water and a large brush
lessons.starter: Dip the brush in water and paint a line on the ground. Say "Look, a wet line. It will dry in the sun."
teacherActivities: Make a big line with the brush. Draw a big circle with chalk.
Give each child a brush and let them paint on the ground.
Give each child chalk and let them draw big marks.
learnerActivities: Children watch and look at the marks.
Child paints a line or a shape.
Child draws marks with chalk.
Child says a word or points.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Make a big line with the brush. Draw a big circle with chalk. Children: Children watch and look at the marks.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a brush and let them paint on the ground. Children: Child paints a line or a shape.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child chalk and let them draw big marks. Children: Child draws marks with chalk.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What did you make?" Children: Child says a word or points.

practical.title: Ground painting
steps: Go to a safe paved area outside.
Paint with water and draw with chalk.
Watch the water marks dry in the sun.
practical.safety: Stay away from the road and check the ground for sharp objects. Use hats in strong sun and wash hands after chalk.

differentiation.support: Hold the brush together and move across the ground.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to draw a long line from one end to the other.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What are you making?
questions.expected: A line, a circle or a word.

expectedOutcomes: Makes big marks with chalk or water
Says a word about their marks
lessons.conclusion: Look at the marks together and wave goodbye to them.
lessons.homeConnection: Draw on a path with chalk or paint with water at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make big marks with chalk and water on the ground" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Crayons on big paper
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will make marks with fat crayons on big paper.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can squeeze, roll and thread and enjoy exploring materials with their hands.
resources: A long sheet of paper taped to the floor
lessons.starter: Tape a long sheet of paper on the floor and make a big scribble with a crayon. Say "I made marks. You try."
teacherActivities: Show how to hold a fat crayon in your fist. Make marks on the paper.
Let each child kneel at the paper and make marks.
Write the child’s word beside their marks.
learnerActivities: Children watch and hold their crayons.
Child makes marks with arm movements.
Child says a word or shows a gesture.
Child watches and says the word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to hold a fat crayon in your fist. Make marks on the paper. Children: Children watch and hold their crayons.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child kneel at the paper and make marks. Children: Child makes marks with arm movements.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Tell me about your marks." Children: Child says a word or shows a gesture.
Step 4. Teacher: Write the child’s word beside their marks. Children: Child watches and says the word.

practical.title: Big paper marks
steps: Tape a long sheet of paper to the floor.
Children kneel and make marks with fat crayons.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic crayons and keep crayons out of mouths. Tape the paper down to prevent slipping.

differentiation.support: Hold the crayon together and move it across the paper.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to draw a line and a circle on the paper.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What did you draw?
questions.expected: A line, a circle or a name for the picture.

questions.question: What colour is your crayon?
questions.expected: Child names or points to the colour.

lessons.conclusion: Put the crayons back in the tin and look at the paper.
lessons.homeConnection: Give your child a big sheet of paper and a fat crayon at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make marks with fat crayons on big paper" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Tell me about my marks
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will talk about their marks and say what they show.
successCriteria: Says a word about their marks
Points to a part of the picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can squeeze, roll and thread and enjoy exploring materials with their hands.
resources: Marks made earlier in the week
lessons.starter: Show a child’s paper from earlier and say "Look at these marks. Tell me about them."
teacherActivities: Sit with a child and look at their marks. Ask "What did you make?"
Repeat the child’s words and write them beside the marks.
Let the child make another picture and tell you about it.
Share a picture with the group.
learnerActivities: Child says a word or points.
Child watches and nods.
Child draws and tells you.
Child shows and says a word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sit with a child and look at their marks. Ask "What did you make?" Children: Child says a word or points.
Step 2. Teacher: Repeat the child’s words and write them beside the marks. Children: Child watches and nods.
Step 3. Teacher: Let the child make another picture and tell you about it. Children: Child draws and tells you.
Step 4. Teacher: Share a picture with the group. Children: Child shows and says a word.

practical.title: Mark talk
steps: Give each child paper and a crayon.
Make a picture and tell a friend about it.
Write a word beside each picture.
practical.safety: Keep crayons out of mouths and supervise sharing. Use non-toxic materials only.

differentiation.support: Point to the marks and offer words for the child to choose.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell you a short sentence about the picture.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is this?
questions.expected: The child’s name for the picture.

expectedOutcomes: Shows a picture to a friend
lessons.conclusion: Put the pictures on the wall and say "Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to tell you about their drawings and write what they say.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "talk about their marks and say what they show" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 marks check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child makes marks and talks about them.
successCriteria: Says a word about their marks
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can squeeze, roll and thread and enjoy exploring materials with their hands.
lessons.starter: Show three mark-making stations and say "Today we make marks."
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: sand, chalk and crayons.
Watch each child make marks and ask "What did you make?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every five minutes.
Child says a word.
Children wash hands and tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: sand, chalk and crayons. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Watch each child make marks and ask "What did you make?" Children: Child says a word.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Mark stations
practical.safety: Supervise sand and water carefully. Use non-toxic chalk and crayons and wash hands.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and offer two tools.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to draw a pattern.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: makes marks with a tool; uses big arm movements; says a word about their marks.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
lessons.homeConnection: Make marks in sand, flour or on paper at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child makes marks and talks about them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
